summary: One cell, covering Figma's Table Cell and Cell Text together. `header` decides <th> versus <td>.
useWhen: every cell in a Table, header or data

useInstead.when: the content is a status label
useInstead.why: put it inside the cell — the cell is the container, not the label

col.use: a column header — inferred inside TableHead

row.use: a row header, e.g. the name column — inferred for a `header` cell in TableBody

colgroup.use: a header spanning several columns, with colspan

rowgroup.use: a header spanning several rows, with rowspan

trailing.use: numbers, currency and dates, so digits line up column-wise

default.use: the default — body text and icon colours

link.use: recolours the content to `text/link` / `icon/primary` for a cell whose content navigates

guarantees: `scope` is inferred when omitted — `col` in TableHead, `row` in TableBody — and can be set explicitly when the inference is wrong
`header` decides the element directly rather than a `type` prop that could disagree with where the cell sits
requires: `scope="col"` on header cells — inferred inside TableHead, but explicit for a header rendered outside it

antiPatterns.dont: `variant="link"` on a cell with no link in it
antiPatterns.why: link-coloured text that does nothing is the clearest possible false affordance
digits stop lining up, so the column can no longer be scanned for magnitude
it is a column rule, not a row rule — on every cell it becomes a grid
